collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE V: FAMILY DRAMA, FEUDS AND LEADERSHIP DISPUTES (LCE-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
All sorts of real-life drama suited to Isola: parents with opinions about who their children marry, arranged matches, inheritances, feuds between families, accusations, apologies that are not enough, and arguments about who should lead.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The leader wants to cut the old grove for a new meeting hut, and villagers plan a protest song: sing it, or ask for a meeting.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The {@chief} has decided to cut down the old grove to build a bigger meeting hut. Many villagers love that grove. (subject) has written a protest song and wants to sing it outside the {@chief}'s hut with everyone who agrees. (friend) thinks the {@chief} might listen to a simple meeting instead. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: Forty villagers gather and sing the protest song outside the {@chief}'s hut. The {@chief} comes out, listens to the whole thing, and says it is a very good song. Then (other.he/she) agrees to build the meeting hut somewhere else. (subject) is almost disappointed it was so easy.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) asks for a meeting. The {@chief} listens politely and says the decision is made. (friend) comes back angry. The next week, forty villagers sing outside the {@chief}'s hut anyway. This time the {@chief} listens.
